correctness.rationale: For each fixed integer \(n\ge4\), represent the random permutation by ranks of iid continuous observations, making local pattern indicators bounded and 2-dependent. Count 4! and 5! overlapping order types to obtain the exact matrix affine in n. Exact action on an orthogonal six-vector basis gives the characteristic roots and proves rank five. The bounded eigenmode telescopes to independent endpoint ascents, and positive limiting eigenvalues on the four complementary modes prove uniqueness. Finite-dependent Cramér–Wold CLT proves the singular four-dimensional Gaussian limit. The embedded checker exhaustively validates 46,224 permutations through order eight and rational identities through order nineteen; these are checks, not substitutes for the argument.

value.rationale: Complete covariance spectra of the six local triple order patterns distinguish global histogram constraints from a genuinely local telescoping boundary mode. The theorem gives exact finite-sample variance calibration, a unique nonconstant bounded-variance contrast, and the full four-dimensional Gaussian covariance in the first nontrivial adjacent-pattern length. It addresses a concrete case of the constrained-pattern degeneracy question singled out by Janson, with mathematical significance independent of any computational table alone.
